validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION confirmed. This is WBI Energy Transmission, Inc.'s FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural gas transmission system (Docket No. CP17-257, FERC order 162 FERC P 61,126, issued 2018-02-15: 'WBI Energy... is a natural gas company that engages in transportation and storage of natural gas in interstate commerce, subject to the Commission's jurisdiction. WBI Energy's pipeline system traverses portions of North Dakota, South Dakota, Montana, and Wyoming.' -- and footnote 3: 'WBI Energy was formerly known as Williston Basin Interstate Pipeline Company.'). Independently corroborated by WBI Energy's own site (wbienergy.com/about) and by the en.wikipedia.org stub 'Williston Basin Pipeline' (reached via the wiki page's own bit.ly citation, which resolves to Wikipedia, not to abarrelfull -- confirmed by following the redirect). Correctly classified transmission (not gathering/distribution): FERC calls it an NGA section 7(c)-jurisdictional interstate transportation/storage system; PipelineType='transmission' and Fuel='Gas' both confirmed. NOT a duplicate of any other roster row: Bison (P0158) delivers INTO this system's interconnects but is a separately FERC-certificated TransCanada/TC Energy pipeline; Northern Border (P2099), Valley Expansion (P0367), the five North Bakken Expansion segments (P3584-P3588), Traill County (P3158) and Doosan Bobcat (P0306) are each distinct FERC dockets/laterals within or adjacent to the broader WBI/MDU network, not restatements of this row -- the CP17-257 order itself distinguishes WBI Energy's 'existing Sheyenne Subsystem' and named laterals from the mainline, consistent with GEM tracking them as separate PIDs. validity.recommendation: update Operator to the current legal/trade name 'WBI Energy Transmission, Inc.' -- the sheet's 'Williston Basin Interstate Pipeline Co' is the entity's FORMER name
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Operator field reads 'Williston Basin Interstate Pipeline Co.' FERC Docket No. CP17-257 (Order Issuing Certificate, issued 2018-02-15), footnote 3, states directly: 'WBI Energy is a wholly-owned subsidiary of WBI Energy, Inc., which is an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of MDU Resources Group, Inc. WBI Energy was formerly known as Williston Basin Interstate Pipeline Company.' Independently, WBI Energy's own About page confirms the same corporate lineage: 'The pipeline system was renamed to "Williston Basin Interstate Pipeline" in 1985, and later became "WBI Energy, Inc." in 2012' (the FERC-regulated transmission subsidiary trades today as WBI Energy Transmission, Inc.). Two independent origins (a federal regulator's finding vs. the operator's own history page) agree the sheet's Operator value is a legal name the entity stopped using in 2012 -- a stale-ownership defect of exactly the kind this batch was told to expect. Owner1='WBI Energy' 100% is NOT contested -- it is consistent with both sources (WBI Energy, Inc. is the immediate parent of the FERC-regulated pipeline subsidiary, itself under MDU Resources Group).

validity.recommendation: verify and likely correct StartYear1 from 1920 to 1929 (or research further to pin the exact year the Glendive-Williston/Baker-Bismarck lines that gave the system its name entered service)
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records StartYear1=1920 with no source. Two independent accounts of MDU Resources' early history place the ACTUAL construction of the transmission lines that gave this system its 'Williston Basin' name several years later than 1920, and disagree with each other on the exact year of the FIRST event: WBI Energy's own About page says the company's gas business began with 'the 1920s' generally and specifically cites '1926 first well and pipeline to Glendive' (Cabin Creek well + a short local line feeding a power plant in eastern Montana -- not yet an interstate transmission system). Referenceforbusiness.com's MDU Resources corporate history is more specific and directly names the pipeline: 'In 1929 the company committed $8 million for a 90-mile line to connect Glendive, Montana, with Williston, North Dakota, and a 220-mile line from the Baker Field site to Bismarck, North Dakota' -- this 90-mile Glendive-to-Williston line is almost certainly the origin of the 'Williston Basin' name and the earliest genuinely interstate-scale transmission construction in the lineage GEM is tracking, six years after the sheet's recorded 1920 and three years after the 1926 Cabin Creek well. Both the 1926 well/local-line event and the 1929 transmission-line event are real and sourced, but NEITHER is '1920,' and the sheet gives no indication which milestone it intended. I'm flagging 1929 as the better-evidenced candidate (it is the event that produced an actual cross-border transmission pipeline named for Williston) but this deserves a closer look before pasting -- e.g. a period MDU/Montana-Dakota Utilities annual report or a state PSC record could pin it exactly. Searched for a second, fully independent (non-history-page) source for either year -- e.g. a period Federal Power Commission record -- and did not find one in the time available; both sources here ultimately draw on the same corporate lineage, so I'm rating this medium rather than high despite two distinct publishers.

WBI Energy's own materials give inconsistent SYSTEM-WIDE totals across different years/documents: the About page (current) states '2.9 Bcf/day transportation capacity' for the ~3,800-mile system; a 2021 WBI Energy Transmission presentation to the Williston Basin (per search-result snippet, not independently re-fetched and read in full this pass) references '~3,600 miles... 2.2 Bcf/day.' Both bracket but do not match 2,100 MMcf/d, and both are SYSTEM totals (transmission+gathering+storage across all of WBI's territory, including named laterals tracked as separate GEM rows like Valley Expansion and the North Bakken Expansion segments) rather than a figure isolable to just the row GEM calls 'Williston Basin Gas Pipeline.' This is the aggregate-vs-segment ambiguity called out in the batch brief: I cannot rule out that 2,100 MMcf/d is a legitimate historical or mainline-only figure, but I also cannot independently confirm it, so I'm filing this as a spec concern rather than adding it as a confirmed ref. Recommend a FERC Form 2 pull or a direct WBI capacity-postings check (transmission.wbienergy.com/informational_postings/capacity/) for a mainline-specific number before this cell is treated as sourced.
